audit.note: Independent re-audit after repair cycle 1, against the pre-repair record and the previous audit note, at both placements (Emergency Governance; Disputes & Emergency Controls, a leaf at both). Requirements: (1) Ending stays here in general: para 4 keeps expiry, ratification ('be ratified by ordinary governance and so become an ordinary decision'), reversal, sunset and revocation with the lapse-versus-stand failure direction, none of it phrased in terms of code; Emergency Upgrades' para 4 adds only what is specific to code (no self-lapse, revert is itself an upgrade and restores the flaw), so the split is clean. (2) The grant-source claim is now conditional: 'Where ordinary governance makes the grant, the power is a delegation from that process; where the power was fixed when the system was deployed, governance can limit or end it only as far as the deployed code allows.' Para 4 matches it ('where the grant provides for it, ordinary governance can revoke it'), and the definition ('grants in advance') holds in both cases. (3) American English: no British forms; spellingProblems is clean; 'afterwards' is used in American English too and appears 27 times in the corpus. (4) Depth: the pass made small trims ('The authority granted' to 'The authority'; the 'switching a price source' example removed; 'parts that were never at risk' to 'parts never at risk'; the approvals clause shortened to 'powers that can alter more usually require more independent approvals to invoke'; 'since ... rather than' recast with a colon; 'through what happens after the power is used' to 'through review after the use'). P2's 'can confirm or undo what it does and can take it back' was dropped from P2 as a repetition, since para 4 covers ratification, reversal and revocation. Words went from 732 to 734: the conditional clause added roughly what the trims removed. Keeping the rest is justified, because each paragraph carries one claim (kinds and scope; the distinction from ordinary governance; holder, conditions and evidence; ending; accountability) and nothing restates the parent or a sibling. Nothing necessary was lost: the 'freezing a balance' correction from the earlier audit is still in place, and the hedges 'commonly', 'usually', 'on a public ledger', 'may reopen' and 'only if revocation does not depend on the holder's cooperation' are kept, as are 'review needs force' and the point that review asks about authority, not cause. No new inaccuracy or contradiction. The narrower 'review after the use' in para 3 points ahead to para 5, which says what review must be able to change. Quality contract section B: the record is accurate with conditions stated, at L2 level, and does not duplicate the parent. The parent's stop-is-safest ranking and lapse-unless-confirmed point are not restated; the record adds the downside of lapse-by-default. Canonical at both placements, no positional or time-sensitive words, prose only (5 paragraphs) as designed. Territory: the four claims are covered; excludes are only named (guardian as a holder; pause, upgrade and breaker mechanics are not developed; measurable conditions are enforced in code without breaker states). Density remarks, none of them a defect: the parallel triples in para 3 (conditions: exploit, private report, failed dependency; evidence: transactions, reproduction, readings) could be cut to one set, but they tie each kind of evidence to its condition. The closing clause of para 4, 'a faster path into the system than anyone else has', is mildly rhetorical but names the failure mode. Verdict: requirements met, no defect, audit recorded.

audit.note: Independent re-audit after repair cycle 1 (American English and editorial-depth pass). Sentence-by-sentence comparison with the pre-repair record: P1 unchanged except 'is found in ... not in' -> 'depends on ... not on'; role check, role-admin self-grant and upgrade-path bypass kept. P2 opening now names the two bounds (threshold, time limit) directly; the 'threshold of two or more' condition on the single-key claim is kept; role expiry versus per-action maximum duration kept ('without further steps' -> 'on its own', same meaning); the limit on judgment is kept, folded into one sentence. P3 drops only the forward pointer 'its bounds trade them against one another', which the next paragraph states; capture, collusion (no outsider, correlated signers, separate organizations) and absence (time zones, lost keys, broken signing tools, expired role) kept. audit.note: Independent re-audit after repair cycle 1, against the pre-repair record and the previous audit note, at both placements (Emergency Governance; Upgrade Security, a leaf at both). Boundary: the general ending and accountability material is gone. P4 no longer lists 'whether the conditions for using the path held' as part of ratification, and P5 no longer lists declaring narrow conditions, publishing each use with its justification or requiring ratification within a fixed period as drift defenses; these are now only named in one clause ('the declared conditions, disclosure and ratification that bound any emergency power'), which Emergency Powers explains. What is specific to replacing code is kept: replaced code stays live until another upgrade replaces it, unlike a pause that can be built to lapse; where no explicit vote is required, inaction leaves the emergency code in place; ratification is the public review of code that has already run (what was deployed, whether it did only what was declared); reverting is itself an upgrade and restores the flaw, so rejection generally needs a replacement fix; and scope confinement is the drift defense specific to this path. The governance-inaction clause is stated as the code-specific default (code does not lapse), not as Emergency Powers' general lapse-versus-stand analysis. American English: no British forms; spellingProblems is clean; 'afterwards' no longer appears. Depth: 831 -> 759 words, five paragraphs, prose only as designed. Sentence-by-sentence: P1 drops 'distinct from whoever holds the ordinary upgrade keys' (covered by 'often held by a different party') and the closing 'What users give up...' sentence (already stated by the ordinary path's read-and-exit contrast and 'skips both the public proposal and the delay'); the declared conditions and the reason the delay is skipped for a private report are kept. P2 is unchanged in substance: pre-agreed patches, private review under the same secrecy, the threshold as review only if signers read the code, scope confinement versus inability to change authority, threshold or delay (the earlier repair splitting these is intact). P3 keeps the 'can accept' wording (earlier repair 4), the insider and reporter sources and the 'neither removes the possibility' hedge. P4 keeps 'which can be built to lapse' (earlier repair 5). P5 drops the 'minor bug fix' example; 'changes that can be framed as urgent' (earlier repair 6) is kept. Earlier repairs 1 and 2 ('governed by different rules and often held by a different party'; 'points that fit before or within the emergency') are intact. Both model claims are still explained: the review an emergency still allows (pre-agreed patches, signer thresholds, narrowed scope, all P2) and ratifying or reverting afterwards (P4). Nothing technically necessary was lost and no hedge was dropped. No new inaccuracy, contradiction or unclear pronoun ('as though it had approved' refers to governance). Quality contract section B: accurate and conditional, L2 level. Neither parent's sentence is restated (Emergency Governance: captured-guardian danger; Upgrade Security: least review, most pressure, key theft). Excludes are not explained (timelocks are not named and the ordinary delay appears only as the contrast the first claim needs; upgrade keys are no longer named; guardians, proxy upgrade risks, upgrade verification and protocol upgrades are not explained). No positional or time-sensitive words, and the record is valid as an emergency power and as an upgrade-security risk. Density remarks, none of them a defect: (1) 'that bound any emergency power' reads slightly broader than intended, since not every power carries ratification; 'that can bound any emergency power' would be more exact. (2) 'Unlike a pause, which can be built to lapse, replaced code stays live' compares a pause with code rather than with an upgrade, but it reads clearly. (3) P2 remains the densest paragraph; the bridge 'Narrowed scope limits what any of this can miss' could fold into the next sentence. No parent or sibling repetition remains to remove.

resolutions.resolution: Not a defect. Emergency Powers is named once in P5 ('the declared conditions, disclosure and ratification that bound any emergency power') to point to the general bounds it owns. Nothing about its kinds, invocation, ending or accountability is explained. This is the boundary decision applied.
Not a defect. Parameter changes appear only as one example of a non-urgent change drawn onto the emergency path ('a parameter change a partner is waiting for'); they are named, not explained.
Not a defect. Security councils appear only as an example holder of the fast path ('such as a security council or an emergency multisig'); their composition and mandate are not explained.

Not a defect. I checked the same four absolutes as the previous audit. 'cannot wait for the ordinary delay' is the definition's condition. 'a path unable to change who holds upgrade authority, its own threshold or the ordinary delay cannot use that change to remove the controls' holds by construction. audit.note: Independent re-audit after repair cycle 1 (American English, editorial-depth pass). Compared before and now sentence by sentence: 1039 to 984 words, five paragraphs, state block unchanged (Normal, Tripped, Testing; trip on threshold within window, test after cooldown, reset when the trial holds, trip again when it fails) and still adds the transition structure the prose only refers to. Window, fixed-window edge doubling, rolling-window cost, absolute/relative/volatility threshold forms, multilevel thresholds, oscillation and cooldown backoff, open/half-open vocabulary all retained. New wording checked: 'activity kept just under it never trips the breaker' replaces 'does not trip the breaker however long it continues'; it is the same claim (a rate measure kept below its threshold cannot trip on that measure) and the following clause makes volume an added measure, so not a new overclaim. 'tripped the breaker' replaces an ambiguous 'it', improving pronoun clarity. Section B: accurate and conditional; L2 level; no parent restatement (Emergency Governance's same-block response and threshold-gaming point are extended, not repeated); siblings and excludes only named (pause mechanism as the actuator of a halt, outflow limit as what a throttle can resemble); 'execution systems' replaces 'autonomous execution systems', which removes the earlier domain-naming signal and still reads correctly at the Execution Recovery placement; holds at all five placements (governance, security incident response, execution recovery, autonomous security responses, economic resilience) with protocol, agent and market examples; no positional or time-sensitive words; American English (no British forms). Possible further trims, not defects: the paired market-wide index and single-stock halt examples could become one, and the window paragraph's one-block/long-window contrast is slightly expansive; neither repeats parent or sibling territory.

Not a defect. 'A halt can be carried out by triggering the system's pause mechanism' names the excluded concept as the actuator a halt may use; no pause-mechanisms claim (granularity, accrual and reconciliation, pause/unpause asymmetry, unliftable or griefing pauses) is explained, and the failure to reset is stated as the breaker's own reset condition.

groupAudit.note: Independent group re-audit after repair cycle 1 (American English and editorial-depth pass on all five owned members). Read the five current records side by side with the parent (Emergency Governance), the dual-role sibling Incident Response, the plan's claims and excludes (unchanged by the cycle), and the pre-cycle records; group signals report 0. No group-level defect; no reopening. Boundary decision (Emergency Powers owns how a power or one use ends, and the conditions, evidence and review of a use; Emergency Upgrades keeps only what is specific to replacing code): applied and holding. Emergency Powers keeps expiry, ratification, reversal, the direction of failure under governance inaction, sunset and revocation (P4) and disclosure, justification and review (P5). Emergency Upgrades no longer lists 'whether the conditions for using the path held' under ratification or 'declaring narrow conditions, publishing each use, requiring ratification within a fixed period' as drift defences; it now points to 'the declared conditions, disclosure and ratification that bound any emergency power' and keeps only code-specific consequences: a public queue reveals the flaw, replaced code cannot be built to lapse so inaction leaves it live, ratification is the postponed public review of code that has already run, reverting is itself an upgrade and restores the flaw, scope that cannot touch its own threshold or the delay, and drift onto the path. The one surviving echo is the inaction point (EP: a change that stands until reversed stays while governance is slow; EU: replaced code stays live as though approved); EU's version follows from code not lapsing, so it specializes rather than restates. Its example conditions (exploit in progress, privately reported vulnerability) repeat two of EP's three, but EU's claim includes 'under which conditions' for the code path and the sentence exists to give the code-specific reason the delay is skipped. Nothing EU relies on was removed from EP: declared conditions (P3), ratification (P4) and disclosure (P5) are all present. Pairs checked. (1) Emergency Powers / Guardians: EP names a guardian only as a possible holder; Guardians owns mechanical bounds, failure modes, appointment, override and removal. Two parallels remain, both inside planned claims: a two-level time limit (EP: power sunset vs action expiry and what inaction does; Guardians: role expiry vs per-action maximum duration as code enforcement, its claimed 'time limit' bound), and 'revocation works only if it does not depend on the holder's cooperation' (one clause in EP) vs 'removal works only if the guardian cannot obstruct it' made concrete with cancelled proposals and a paused executor. General/specific pairing, not leakage; the shared 'works only if' wording is a minor echo. EP's new P2 sentence (a power fixed at deployment can be limited or ended by governance only as far as the code allows) agrees with Guardians' conditional 'where ordinary governance appoints' and 'where governance holds administrative authority over the guardian's role'. (2) Pause Mechanisms / Circuit Breakers: Pause names a breaker only as a party that can pause; Breakers names the pause only as the actuator a halt may use and states what makes a halt part of a breaker. Both describe a stop that fails to end, from different causes (unpause role renounced, keys lost, unpause depends on paused contracts vs reset awaiting a confirmation or a test on a quantity that cannot recover while halted); reopening is treated from different angles (accrual reconciliation and who acts first vs a test re-tripping on held-back demand); deliberate trips by an outsider (Breakers) differ from griefing by the pause holder (Pause). (3) Emergency Powers / Pause Mechanisms: EP's 'power to stop' is one kind of authority; Pause owns granularity, accrual, asymmetry and unliftable or griefing pauses; EP's 'more power, more approvals' agrees with Pause's cheap pause and expensive unpause. (4) Guardians / Pause Mechanisms: both note that pausing the contracts through which governance executes can block governance, as a cause of an unliftable pause vs as obstruction of the guardian's own removal; each within its claim. (5) Guardians / Emergency Upgrades: both treat signer thresholds, from different facets (independence against capture and collusion vs threshold as review that fails when signers approve a description); EU's scope that cannot change who holds upgrade authority and Guardians' role administration and upgrade path as the real reach are complementary. (6) Each member / Incident Response: EP separates review of the authority from finding the cause (post-mortem left to IR); Guardians' drills address signer absence, not response preparation generally; Pause's 'needs no diagnosis' and EU's private review do not explain detection, containment or disclosure; Breakers names IR only via the parent. Contradictions: none. Lapse is consistent across members and parent (Pause: a pause that does not lapse on its own, lapse limits little against re-pausing; EU: unlike a pause, which can be built to lapse; Guardians: per-action maximum duration; EP: both defaults and their failure directions). Terms consistent: ordinary governance, holder, signers, signer threshold (Guardians, EU, Pause) vs measured threshold (Breakers only, never mixed within a record), security council, ratify, revoke, lift/unpause, trip/test/reset; 'revert' (restore prior code) vs 'reverse' (undo an action) used accurately.
